newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish farmers call for interest rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Irish farmers call for interest rate cut.

text.p: The Irish Farmers' Association has called for a one percentage point cut in Irish interest rates to counter a soaring Irish pound.
The punt is currently trading at the top of the ERM grid, nearly 11 percent above the French franc, the weakest currency.

"The policy by the government and the central bank in keeping Irish interest rates at about 2.5 percent above German and French rates and close to UK rates is distorting the value of the Irish pound," the IFA said in a statement released on Tuesday.

"An immediate one percent cut in interest rates is now essential in order to achieve an Irish pound exchange rate which is fair to the exporting sectors of the economy including the agri-food sector," it said.

IFA president John Donnelly said the Irish pound was overvalued by about 10 percent relative to the Ecu, which is particularly relevant to agriculture price levels, and by at least five percent on a trade-weighted basis.

"We all know that market forces are tending to link the Irish pound with a very strong sterling but government policy on interest rates should seek to counter these trends rather than reinforce them," Donnelly said.
The IFA said the agri-food sector was seeking to overcome the BSE crisis in the beef industry and an overvalued Irish pound was the last thing it needed.
It also called on the government to match the amount provided under the EU compensatory aid mechanism to temporarily reduce the losses from green pound revaluations.
